title: Dispatch: graded exhaustion through adjust_exhaustion (attempt 1)
description:
Implements capability bead eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.3 (read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.3`). Integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 (single PR for eight beads). Your branch already contains the suffocation gate (0032), combatant death rules (0033: death_rules, dying/stable statuses), and the nonlethal knockout — read hpLifecycle.ts and encounterCombatants.ts in full first. NO migration in this child (exhaustion lives in conditions_json). Read AGENTS.md; docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendment A5; ADR 0020 §§2-3; the condition:exhaustion record in the committed pack (levels 1-6; levelApplication current-and-lower); state/domainMutations.ts addCondition; state/rest.ts applyExhaustion (long-rest reduction, accepts id 'exhaustion' or legacy 'exhausted').

SOURCE (condition:exhaustion): "Exhaustion is measured in six levels. An effect can give a creature one or more levels of exhaustion ... If an already exhausted creature suffers another effect that causes exhaustion, its current level of exhaustion increases by the amount specified ... An effect that removes exhaustion reduces its level as specified ..., with all exhaustion effects ending if a creature's exhaustion level is reduced below 1." Level 4: "Hit point maximum halved". Level 6: "Death". rule:water: "If the character already has one or more levels of exhaustion, the character takes two levels in either case."

DESIGN (decided by the supervisor; implement exactly):
1. New tool `adjust_exhaustion` (mutates) { delta: non-zero integer from -6 to 6, character? | combatantId? (mutually exclusive; exactly one target, character defaulting as other character tools do) }. One transaction. Reads the current level (absent = 0; normalize a legacy 'exhausted' id to 'exhaustion'); new level = clamp(current + delta, 0, 6); level 0 removes the entry; otherwise the entry is {id:'exhaustion', level}. The model passes the number of levels the source effect specifies (a declared input, like a modifier); the engine owns the sum, the clamp, and the consequences. Result reports previous level, new level, and consequences.
2. Level 6 is death, applied by the engine in the same transaction: character → the hpLifecycle death transition (add an exported helper there if none exists; it must run the existing death side effects: attunement end, concentration break 'dead', stable-recovery cleared; do not duplicate them); combatant → status 'dead' through the updateCombatant path so its concentration cleanup and actor sync run.
3. Level 4+ halves the hit point maximum, derived not stored: add one helper (e.g. effectiveHpMax(row)) = floor(hp_max / 2) when the exhaustion level >= 4, else hp_max, and use it everywhere the HP rules read the maximum — character: healing cap, instant-death overflow comparison, temp-HP rules if they reference max, status rendering (formatHpStatus and the context/roster lines); combatant: updateCombatant healing clamp, player-character instant-death comparison (from 0033), roster rendering. Entering level >= 4 clamps current HP to the effective maximum in the same transaction (no death from the clamp itself: HP cannot drop below 1 from the clamp unless already 0). Leaving level 4 removes the cap without healing. Do NOT mutate the stored hp_max (level-up and other code own it). grep for every read of hp_max / hpMax in src to catch the rule-bearing ones; leave purely informational uses alone only if they are not rules.
4. Long rest: rest.ts applyExhaustion keeps its existing behaviour (reduce by 1 when food and drink were ingested); make it use the same normalization helper. Reducing below 4 removes the cap automatically because it is derived.
5. add_condition / update_combatant addCondition: they keep their no-op-on-existing-id contract, but adding an 'exhaustion'/'exhausted' condition through them must now be refused with an error that points to adjust_exhaustion (so the level path is single-owner). Update their descriptions accordingly (remove the "a later level increase cannot be recorded" sentence from add_condition).
6. adjust_exhaustion description: contracts only (levels clamp at 6; level 6 is death; at level 4 or higher the engine halves the hit point maximum; level below 1 removes exhaustion). Levels 1-3 and 5 (disadvantage, speed) are not applied by the engine — they are declared by the DM on rolls and in narration; say "the engine applies the level 4 and level 6 effects; the other levels' effects are declared on the relevant rolls" — no per-rule prose.
7. Known limits (ruleKnownLimits.ts), R0 re-derivation for rule:food, rule:water, rule:speed (shared helper exhaustionLevelLimit): the trap is gone. Retire the three entries if nothing misleading remains, or rewrite to a bounded statement only if a real trap remains (e.g. that exhaustion is recorded only through adjust_exhaustion with the levels the rule imposes, two for rule:water when already exhausted). Supervisor preference: keep a short bounded statement naming adjust_exhaustion for each (it is the single write path and add_condition now refuses it), with rule:water stating the source's two-level case as the delta to pass. Remove 'graded-exhaustion-increase' from ENGINE_CAPABILITY_GAPS and all capabilityGaps. Participants validated. Update the identity-pinned gapsByKey map and the exhaustion assertions in packages/core/test/rules/ruleAwareness.test.ts and tools.test.ts (replace the 'cannot currently be persisted' / no-substitute assertions with assertions on the new contract; keep a regression that no statement suggests remove_condition + re-add). Keep the 8-word source-restatement test green. Design doc A5 table: note the gap as landed in eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.3.

TESTS: absent→+1, +2 on existing, clamp at 6 → death (character life_state dead with attunement/concentration side effects; combatant dead with concentration cleanup), negative delta incl. removal below 1, level 4 halves effective max and clamps current HP, healing capped at effective max, instant-death comparison uses effective max, leaving level 4 restores the cap, legacy 'exhausted' normalized, add_condition/update_combatant refuse exhaustion, long rest reduction still works, tool-registry invocation for both targets.

OUT OF SCOPE: speed or disadvantage automation; anything not listed.

TEST COVERAGE IS PART OF THE DELIVERABLE: write every test listed under TESTS (one `it` per bullet at minimum), driven through the real tool registry wherever the behaviour is model-facing. The supervisor reviews the test list against this spec and rejects under-tested work. In your completion notes, map each TESTS bullet to the test name that covers it.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation per the description on its own branch; npm run verify:worktree green before commit; completion report in bd notes; bead closed by the child.
notes:
Dispatched gpt-6-luna high, pgid 2513197, off eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8@0d5ad3cd.
Completion report (commit b8e2b89b). Files changed: added adjust_exhaustion tool and atomic exhaustion mutation/helper; updated character HP lifecycle, combatant update/death/healing, long-rest normalization, effective HP display, condition-write refusal, known limits, awareness/tool tests, and A5 design table. Decisions: followed supervisor design; used existing character death writer for attunement/concentration/recovery cleanup and updateCombatant for combatant death/actor sync; no migration and no design deviations. TESTS mapping: absent→+1 and +2 existing + registry character target: exhaustion.test.ts “records +1 from absence and +2 on an existing level through the registry”; clamp at 6 and character dead with concentration/attunement cleanup: “clamps at six and applies the character death transition”; combatant dead/concentration cleanup: “applies level-six death to combatants through updateCombatant”; negative delta/removal below 1: “clamps negative deltas at zero and removes exhaustion below level one”; level 4 effective max/current HP clamp: “halves effective maximum at level four and clamps current HP without changing hp_max”; healing cap: “caps healing at the derived maximum”; character instant-death threshold: “uses the effective maximum for instant-death overflow”; combatant effective healing/death threshold: “caps player-combatant healing and instant-death overflow at the effective maximum”; leaving level 4 does not heal: “removes the derived cap below level four without healing”; legacy exhausted normalization: “normalizes the legacy exhausted id when adjusted”; add_condition/update_combatant refusal: “refuses condition-tool exhaustion writes and points to adjust_exhaustion”; long-rest reduction interop: rest.test.ts “long rest restores HP, temporary HP, resources, half Hit Dice, and one exhaustion level with food” and “does not reduce exhaustion when a long rest lacks food and drink”; registry both targets: character test above plus exhaustion.test.ts “raises a combatant level and applies the effective HP maximum through the registry” and combatant death test above. Rule disclosure/no remove-and-readd regression: ruleAwareness.test.ts “routes exhaustion recording through adjust_exhaustion after R0 re-derivation” and “offers no substitute for a missing deterministic operation”. Verification: npm run verify:worktree passed (format/check, typecheck, 318 test files passed, 2 skipped; 5,619 tests passed, 3 skipped).}
